inputs.abstract:
The goal of this draft is to initiate an overview and hierarchy of graph
parameters. As a first step, we introduce the basic relations for comparing
parameters and define a first batch of thirteen graph parameters.
Throughout, graphs are finite, simple, and undirected.

The comparisons are based on functional boundedness: one parameter bounds
another if the latter is bounded by a total computable nondecreasing function
of the former on every finite simple graph. From this relation, we define
functional equivalence, absence of a functional bound, strict functional
boundedness, and incomparability. We prove that every pair of parameters is
either functionally equivalent, strictly bounded in one of the two
directions, or incomparable, with exactly one of these four cases holding.
We also prove that functional equivalence is an equivalence relation,
strict functional boundedness is a strict partial order, and incomparability
is symmetric and irreflexive.

The first batch consists of the following parameters:

- Arboricity
- Chromatic number
- Clique-width
- Degeneracy
- Distance to cluster graphs
- Distance to cographs
- Distance to complete graphs
- Distance to planar graphs
- Maximum matching number
- Neighborhood diversity
- Twin-cover number
- Vertex clique cover number
- Vertex-cover number

All definitions include disconnected graphs and assign value zero to the
empty graph. This draft provides the definitions and general properties of
the comparison relations; comparisons between the concrete parameters remain
to be added to the hierarchy.

concepts.title: Arboricity
concepts.description:
The arboricity of a graph is the minimum number of forests whose edge sets
partition its edge set. An edgeless graph has arboricity zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Arboricity
type: definition
---
The arboricity of a graph is the minimum number of forests whose edge sets
partition its edge set. An edgeless graph has arboricity zero.
-/

namespace Lax825442.Arboricity

/-- An assignment of graph edges to `k` classes, each inducing a forest. -/
def HasArboricityAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ color : G.edgeSet → Fin k,
    (∀ i : Fin k,
      (G.deleteEdges {e : Sym2 V | ∃ h : e ∈ G.edgeSet,
        color ⟨e, h⟩ ≠ i}).IsAcyclic)

/-- The minimum number of forests partitioning the edges. -/
noncomputable def arboricity {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasArboricityAtMost G k}

end Lax825442.Arboricity

concepts.title: Functional bounds between graph parameters
concepts.description:
For graph parameters $p$ and $q$ with values in the natural numbers, we write
$p\to q$ if there is a total computable nondecreasing function
$f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $q(G)\le f(p(G))$ for every finite
simple graph $G$. Thus, a bound on $p$ yields a bound on $q$. The definition
includes disconnected graphs.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax153141.GraphParameters
import Mathlib.Order.Monotone.Basic
import Mathlib.Computability.Partrec

/-!
---
title: Functional bounds between graph parameters
type: definition
---
For graph parameters $p$ and $q$ with values in the natural numbers, we write
$p\to q$ if there is a total computable nondecreasing function
$f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $q(G)\le f(p(G))$ for every finite
simple graph $G$. Thus, a bound on $p$ yields a bound on $q$. The definition
includes disconnected graphs.
-/

namespace Lax825442.Bounds

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- A computable nondecreasing function of `p` bounds `q` on every finite simple graph. -/
def Bounds (p q : GraphParam) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Computable f ∧ Monotone f ∧
    (∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      q G ≤ f (p G))

end Lax825442.Bounds

concepts.title: Chromatic number
concepts.description:
The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colors needed for a
proper vertex coloring.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.Vertex

/-!
---
title: Chromatic number
type: definition
---
The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colors needed for a
proper vertex coloring.
-/

namespace Lax825442.ChromaticNumber

/-- The natural-valued chromatic number of a finite graph. -/
noncomputable def chromaticNumber {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

end Lax825442.ChromaticNumber

concepts.title: Clique-width
concepts.description:
The clique-width of a graph is the minimum number of labels needed to
construct it using vertex creation, disjoint union, the addition of all edges
between two distinct label classes, and relabeling.
The empty graph has clique-width zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax271696.CliqueExpr
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Maps
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.EquivFin
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Clique-width
type: definition
---
The clique-width of a graph is the minimum number of labels needed to
construct it using vertex creation, disjoint union, the addition of all edges
between two distinct label classes, and relabeling.
The empty graph has clique-width zero.
-/

namespace Lax825442.CliqueWidth

open Lax271696.CliqueExpr

/-- A valid `k`-expression builds a numbered copy of `G`. -/
def HasCliqueWidthAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Fintype.card V = 0 ∨
    ∃ e : Expr (Fintype.card V) k,
      ValidFor e (G.comap (Fintype.equivFin V).symm)

/-- The minimum number of labels in a valid expression for `G`. -/
noncomputable def cliqueWidth {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasCliqueWidthAtMost G k}

end Lax825442.CliqueWidth

concepts.title: Degeneracy
concepts.description:
The degeneracy of a graph is the least natural number $k$ such that every
nonempty induced subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $k$. The degree is
measured within that induced subgraph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Degeneracy
type: definition
---
The degeneracy of a graph is the least natural number $k$ such that every
nonempty induced subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $k$. The degree is
measured within that induced subgraph.
-/

namespace Lax825442.Degeneracy

/-- Every nonempty induced subgraph has a vertex of degree at most `k`. -/
def HasDegeneracyAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset V, S.Nonempty →
    (∃ v : V, v ∈ S ∧
      ({u : V | u ∈ S ∧ G.Adj v u}.ncard ≤ k))

/-- The least degeneracy bound. -/
noncomputable def degeneracy {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasDegeneracyAtMost G k}

end Lax825442.Degeneracy

concepts.title: Distance to complete graphs
concepts.description:
The distance to complete graphs is the minimum number of vertices whose
deletion leaves a complete graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Distance to complete graphs
type: definition
---
The distance to complete graphs is the minimum number of vertices whose
deletion leaves a complete graph.
-/

namespace Lax825442.DistanceToClique

/-- Minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a complete graph. -/
noncomputable def distanceToClique {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset V, (S.card = k) ∧
    (G.induce {v | v ∉ S} = ⊤)}

end Lax825442.DistanceToClique

concepts.title: Distance to cluster graphs
concepts.description:
The distance to cluster graphs is the minimum number of vertices whose
deletion leaves a cluster graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.CompleteMultipartite
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Distance to cluster graphs
type: definition
---
The distance to cluster graphs is the minimum number of vertices whose
deletion leaves a cluster graph.
-/

namespace Lax825442.DistanceToCluster

/-- Minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a disjoint union of cliques. -/
noncomputable def distanceToCluster {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset V, (S.card = k) ∧
    ((G.induce {v | v ∉ S})ᶜ.IsCompleteMultipartite)}

end Lax825442.DistanceToCluster

concepts.title: Absence of a functional bound
concepts.description:
We write $p\not\to q$ if no total computable nondecreasing function bounds
$q(G)$ in terms of $p(G)$ on every finite simple graph. This relation is the
negation of functional boundedness.

A family of graphs on which $p$ is uniformly bounded and $q$ is unbounded
establishes this relation. Such a family is sufficient, but the absence of a
computable bound does not imply the absence of every noncomputable bound.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.Bounds

/-!
---
title: Absence of a functional bound
type: definition
---
We write $p\not\to q$ if no total computable nondecreasing function bounds
$q(G)$ in terms of $p(G)$ on every finite simple graph. This relation is the
negation of functional boundedness.

A family of graphs on which $p$ is uniformly bounded and $q$ is unbounded
establishes this relation. Such a family is sufficient, but the absence of a
computable bound does not imply the absence of every noncomputable bound.
-/

namespace Lax825442.DoesNotBound

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- No computable nondecreasing functional bound from `p` to `q` exists. -/
def DoesNotBound (p q : GraphParam) : Prop :=
  ¬ (Lax825442.Bounds.Bounds p q)

end Lax825442.DoesNotBound

concepts.title: Functional equivalence of graph parameters
concepts.description:
Two graph parameters are functionally equivalent if each is bounded by a
total computable nondecreasing function of the other on every finite simple
graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.Bounds

/-!
---
title: Functional equivalence of graph parameters
type: definition
---
Two graph parameters are functionally equivalent if each is bounded by a
total computable nondecreasing function of the other on every finite simple
graph.
-/

namespace Lax825442.Equivalent

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- Functional bounds hold in both directions. -/
def Equivalent (p q : GraphParam) : Prop :=
  (Lax825442.Bounds.Bounds p q) ∧ (Lax825442.Bounds.Bounds q p)

end Lax825442.Equivalent

concepts.title: Functional equivalence is an equivalence relation
concepts.description:
Functional equivalence of graph parameters is reflexive, symmetric, and
transitive.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.Equivalent

/-!
---
title: Functional equivalence is an equivalence relation
type: theorem
---
Functional equivalence of graph parameters is reflexive, symmetric, and
transitive.
-/

namespace Lax825442.EquivalentEquivalence

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- Mutual functional boundedness is an equivalence relation. -/
axiom equivalent_equivalence : Equivalence Lax825442.Equivalent.Equivalent

end Lax825442.EquivalentEquivalence

statements.doc: Mutual functional boundedness is an equivalence relation.

concepts.title: Incomparability of graph parameters
concepts.description:
Two graph parameters are incomparable if neither is bounded by a total
computable nondecreasing function of the other on every finite simple graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.DoesNotBound

/-!
---
title: Incomparability of graph parameters
type: definition
---
Two graph parameters are incomparable if neither is bounded by a total
computable nondecreasing function of the other on every finite simple graph.
-/

namespace Lax825442.Incomparable

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- Neither parameter functionally bounds the other. -/
def Incomparable (p q : GraphParam) : Prop :=
  (Lax825442.DoesNotBound.DoesNotBound p q) ∧
    (Lax825442.DoesNotBound.DoesNotBound q p)

end Lax825442.Incomparable

concepts.title: Incomparability is symmetric and irreflexive
concepts.description: Incomparability of graph parameters is symmetric and irreflexive.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.Incomparable

/-!
---
title: Incomparability is symmetric and irreflexive
type: theorem
---
Incomparability of graph parameters is symmetric and irreflexive.
-/

namespace Lax825442.IncomparableProperties

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- Incomparability is symmetric and no parameter is incomparable with itself. -/
axiom incomparable_symmetric_irreflexive :
  (Symmetric Lax825442.Incomparable.Incomparable) ∧
    (Irreflexive Lax825442.Incomparable.Incomparable)

end Lax825442.IncomparableProperties

concepts.title: Maximum matching number
concepts.description:
The maximum matching number of a graph is the largest number of edges in a
matching. The empty graph has maximum matching number zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Matching
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

/-!
---
title: Maximum matching number
type: definition
---
The maximum matching number of a graph is the largest number of edges in a
matching. The empty graph has maximum matching number zero.
-/

namespace Lax825442.MaximumMatching

/-- The maximum number of edges in a matching. -/
noncomputable def maximumMatching {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sSup {n : ℕ | ∃ M : G.Subgraph, M.IsMatching ∧ (M.edgeSet.ncard = n)}

end Lax825442.MaximumMatching

concepts.title: Neighborhood diversity
concepts.description:
The neighborhood diversity of a graph is the minimum number of parts in a
partition of its vertex set such that each part induces a clique or an
independent set and is a module: its vertices have the same neighbors outside
the part. The empty graph has neighborhood diversity zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Neighborhood diversity
type: definition
---
The neighborhood diversity of a graph is the minimum number of parts in a
partition of its vertex set such that each part induces a clique or an
independent set and is a module: its vertices have the same neighbors outside
the part. The empty graph has neighborhood diversity zero.
-/

namespace Lax825442.NeighborhoodDiversity

/-- A partition into `k` parts, each a module and each inducing a clique or
an independent set. Empty labels are allowed and disappear at the minimum. -/
def HasNeighborhoodDiversityAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ part : V → Fin k,
    (∀ u v w : V,
      (part u = part v ∧ part w ≠ part u) → (G.Adj u w ↔ G.Adj v w)) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin k,
      (∀ u v : V,
        (u ≠ v ∧ (part u = i ∧ part v = i)) → G.Adj u v) ∨
      (∀ u v : V,
        (part u = i ∧ part v = i) → ¬ G.Adj u v))

/-- The minimum number of neighborhood-diversity parts. -/
noncomputable def neighborhoodDiversity {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasNeighborhoodDiversityAtMost G k}

end Lax825442.NeighborhoodDiversity

concepts.title: Exactly one of four relations for graph parameters
concepts.description:
For every pair of graph parameters, exactly one of four relations holds:
the first strictly bounds the second, the second strictly bounds the first,
the parameters are functionally equivalent, or they are incomparable.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.StrictlyBounds
import Lax825442.Equivalent
import Lax825442.Incomparable

/-!
---
title: Exactly one of four relations for graph parameters
type: theorem
---
For every pair of graph parameters, exactly one of four relations holds:
the first strictly bounds the second, the second strictly bounds the first,
the parameters are functionally equivalent, or they are incomparable.
-/

namespace Lax825442.RelationClassification
open Lax153141.GraphParameters
open Lax825442.StrictlyBounds Lax825442.Equivalent Lax825442.Incomparable

/-- Exactly one of the four cases holds: exhaustiveness and pairwise exclusiveness. -/
axiom relationClassification (p q : GraphParam) :
  (StrictlyBounds p q ∨ StrictlyBounds q p ∨ Equivalent p q ∨ Incomparable p q) ∧
    ¬ (StrictlyBounds p q ∧ StrictlyBounds q p) ∧
    ¬ (StrictlyBounds p q ∧ Equivalent p q) ∧
    ¬ (StrictlyBounds p q ∧ Incomparable p q) ∧
    ¬ (StrictlyBounds q p ∧ Equivalent p q) ∧
    ¬ (StrictlyBounds q p ∧ Incomparable p q) ∧
    ¬ (Equivalent p q ∧ Incomparable p q)

end Lax825442.RelationClassification

concepts.title: Strict functional boundedness of graph parameters
concepts.description:
A graph parameter $p$ strictly bounds a graph parameter $q$ if $q$ is bounded
by a total computable nondecreasing function of $p$ on every finite simple
graph, but $p$ admits no such bound in terms of $q$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.DoesNotBound

/-!
---
title: Strict functional boundedness of graph parameters
type: definition
---
A graph parameter $p$ strictly bounds a graph parameter $q$ if $q$ is bounded
by a total computable nondecreasing function of $p$ on every finite simple
graph, but $p$ admits no such bound in terms of $q$.
-/

namespace Lax825442.StrictlyBounds

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- Functional boundedness holds in one direction and fails in the reverse. -/
def StrictlyBounds (p q : GraphParam) : Prop :=
  (Lax825442.Bounds.Bounds p q) ∧
    (Lax825442.DoesNotBound.DoesNotBound q p)

end Lax825442.StrictlyBounds

concepts.title: Strict functional boundedness is a strict partial order
concepts.description:
Strict functional boundedness of graph parameters is irreflexive and
transitive, and hence is a strict partial order. Asymmetry follows from these
two properties.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825442.StrictlyBounds
import Mathlib.Order.Defs.Unbundled

/-!
---
title: Strict functional boundedness is a strict partial order
type: theorem
---
Strict functional boundedness of graph parameters is irreflexive and
transitive, and hence is a strict partial order. Asymmetry follows from these
two properties.
-/

namespace Lax825442.StrictlyBoundsOrder

open Lax153141.GraphParameters

/-- Strict functional boundedness is an irreflexive, transitive relation. -/
axiom strictlyBounds_strictOrder :
  IsStrictOrder GraphParam Lax825442.StrictlyBounds.StrictlyBounds

end Lax825442.StrictlyBoundsOrder

statements.doc: Strict functional boundedness is an irreflexive, transitive relation.

concepts.title: Twin-cover number
concepts.description:
Two adjacent vertices are true twins if they have the same neighbors outside
the pair. A twin-cover is a set of vertices that meets every edge whose
endpoints are not true twins in the original graph. The twin-cover number is
the minimum size of a twin-cover.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Twin-cover number
type: definition
---
Two adjacent vertices are true twins if they have the same neighbors outside
the pair. A twin-cover is a set of vertices that meets every edge whose
endpoints are not true twins in the original graph. The twin-cover number is
the minimum size of a twin-cover.
-/

namespace Lax825442.TwinCover

/-- Adjacent vertices with the same neighbors outside the pair. -/
def TrueTwins {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (u v : V) : Prop :=
  G.Adj u v ∧ (∀ w : V,
    (w ≠ u ∧ w ≠ v) → (G.Adj u w ↔ G.Adj v w))

/-- A set meeting every edge except those between true twins. -/
def IsTwinCover {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃u v : V⦄,
    (G.Adj u v ∧ ¬ TrueTwins G u v) → (u ∈ S ∨ v ∈ S)

/-- The minimum cardinality of a twin-cover. -/
noncomputable def twinCover {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ S : Set V, (S.ncard = k) ∧ IsTwinCover G S}

end Lax825442.TwinCover

concepts.title: Vertex clique cover number
concepts.description:
The vertex clique cover number of a graph is the minimum number of cliques
whose vertex sets partition its vertex set. Equivalently, it is the chromatic
number of the complement: each color class of the complement is a clique in
the original graph. The empty graph has vertex clique cover number zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.Vertex

/-!
---
title: Vertex clique cover number
type: definition
---
The vertex clique cover number of a graph is the minimum number of cliques
whose vertex sets partition its vertex set. Equivalently, it is the chromatic
number of the complement: each color class of the complement is a clique in
the original graph. The empty graph has vertex clique cover number zero.
-/

namespace Lax825442.VertexCliqueCover

/-- The vertex clique cover number, expressed as the chromatic number of the
complement. -/
noncomputable def vertexCliqueCover {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  Gᶜ.chromaticNumber.toNat

end Lax825442.VertexCliqueCover

concepts.title: Vertex-cover number
concepts.description:
A vertex cover is a set of vertices that meets every edge. The vertex-cover
number is the minimum size of a vertex cover.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.VertexCover

/-!
---
title: Vertex-cover number
type: definition
---
A vertex cover is a set of vertices that meets every edge. The vertex-cover
number is the minimum size of a vertex cover.
-/

namespace Lax825442.VertexCover

/-- The natural-valued vertex-cover number of a finite graph. -/
noncomputable def vertexCover {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  G.vertexCoverNum.toNat

end Lax825442.VertexCover

proofs.description:
The identity function establishes reflexivity. Exchanging the two bounds
establishes symmetry, and composing the bounding functions in both directions
establishes transitivity.

Exchanging the two assertions that no bound exists establishes symmetry.
For irreflexivity, the identity function bounds every parameter by itself,
contradicting the assumption of incomparability.

After unfolding the definitions, classical propositional logic shows that
at least one of the four cases holds and that no two hold simultaneously.

Irreflexivity follows because a strict bound would both assert and deny a
functional bound from a parameter to itself. For transitivity, compose the
forward bounding functions. A bound in the reverse direction would contradict
the first strict comparison.
